opportunities.title: Small grants

amount.raw: Awards generally fall in a range of £1,500-£5,000 and will only exceptionally exceed £6,000. Travel: up to £2,000 per person (up to 13 days) or £2,500 per person (14+ days); up to £5,000 for PhD fieldwork visits of six months or more; Japan office up to ¥300,000.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Applicants must belong to, or provide evidence of support from, an organisation or institution willing to receive grant funds. Applications are not accepted from individuals seeking support for personal projects (though the UK office may consider individuals with proof of organisational support). Grant payments cannot be made to personal bank accounts. No support for undergraduate or master's students, student fees, or travel in connection with study for a qualification (excluding PhD students).
opportunities.summary: Seed funding to enable UK-Japan projects that bring people together to deepen mutual understanding, exchange ideas/expertise, or develop lasting collaboration. Supports festivals, workshops, performances, exchanges, collaborative projects, Japanese language and cultural studies teaching, and academic research/visits/exchange. UK office holds three annual awards meetings; Japan office holds two.

opportunities.title: Butterfield Awards in Medicine and Health

deadlines.raw: 1 December (annual, decision in March of the following year)

amount.raw: Up to £10,000 per year; continuing projects lasting up to three years to a maximum of £10,000 per year, to a total limit of £30,000.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Applicants should normally show an existing research record; consideration also given to practitioners, managers, carers or others in health-related fields establishing working links between organisations or producing a publishable comparative study. Projects must involve partners in both the UK and Japan and be supported by reputable referees not based at the same institution as either partner. Preference to those not previously involved in UK-Japan collaboration and early-career applicants.
opportunities.summary: Annual awards supporting exchanges and collaborations between health and medical professionals in Japan and the UK. Broad in application, supporting study of scientific, clinical, social and economic issues in healthcare, and creating opportunities for researchers, practitioners, policy makers, managers and voluntary sector workers in both countries to share knowledge and develop new approaches. Grants may be used for travel expenses or other costs including conference and publication costs.
